# 1.2.82 - a player's dice start at the GM's card, voice follows a move at once, and a GM's board shows where secret passages lead

Stage E86 in full: H82, the owner's asks of 21.10 and 23.10.2026 after 1.2.80 and 1.2.81 - a wait before a player's dice, a
wait when voice joins a new room, and a GM who sees the passages. A player's drawn roll now starts its dice as the GM's card
arrives, and the GM's own screen throws it at the GM's throw; a player's and an Assistant GM's dice carry the GM's look with no
special effects but the global ones; a character's voice moves to the new room as soon as the move ends; and a GM's board names
where each secret tunnel and stairs end leads and shows, dimmed, where a secret passage cuts a room's outline. No other stage is
in this version. None of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps), and every time below is the test harness's.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **With *One dice look for the table* on, players and Assistant GMs lose their special effects.** At the first sweep after the
   update each of them is held to the GM's dice appearance with an empty special-effects list: effects 1.2.80 or 1.2.81 wrote
   from the GM's list are taken off, and so are effects a player picked for themselves. The GM's own look and effects stay as they
   are, and a full Gamemaster is never written. Effects a Gamemaster marks as global in Dice So Nice still play on a player's
   throw, through Dice So Nice itself, as in 1.2.79, where the browser showing the throw reads them (Known gaps).
3. **Voice moves at once.** A character's voice moves to the new room as soon as the move ends, where 1.2.81 waited 1.5 s after
   the last move of anybody. Two separate moves less than 1.5 s apart now reconnect twice, one after the other (Known gaps).
4. **Settings, keys and texts.** No new setting and no new keybinding; a GM's view of the passages has no switch. `lang/en.json`
   keeps 3704 strings and `lang/pl.json` 4499 (none added, none removed, 1 reworded in each): the hint of *One dice look for the
   table* now reads "Every player and Assistant GM throws Dice So Nice dice in the look of one full Gamemaster, fixed the first
   time the game runs with it on, with no special effects but those a Gamemaster marks as global, and a change of their own goes
   back to it. Another full Gamemaster's own look stays theirs and changes nothing for the table beyond the effects they mark as
   global. Each keeps their own display and performance settings. Switching this off gives nobody their old look back."

## At the table

### For the GM

- **A player's roll reaches your screen sooner.** When a player's action roll or statistic from the sheet is drawn on your
  browser, your screen throws its dice at your throw, before the roll's card is written, where 1.2.81 waited for that card to come
  back from the server. In the harness, with 80 ms added each way on every browser, from the player's Roll to the dice on the
  primary GM's screen: 328 -> 165.5 ms for a statistic from the sheet and 327 -> 165 ms for an action's roll (medians of 10).
- Each roll is still thrown once on your screen, as the player's throw, and without Dice So Nice its sound plays once. A roll
  you refuse throws nothing. An Assistant GM's screen and the incident's audience get the dice as in 1.2.81, with the card.
- With **Verbose console logging** on, a roll whose dice were thrown on your screen and whose card was then not written leaves the
  Debug line "The dice of <player>'s roll were thrown on this screen, and its message was not written: no card stands for them."
- **On your board, under each ring of a secret tunnel or stairs end,** it says, dimmed, "Secret passage to {room}" with the room
  that end leads to by its name, and at a one-way tunnel's way out "Secret passage from {room}" with the room it comes from.
- A one-way tunnel with both ends on the floor carries an arrowhead on its dashed line, pointing to its way out. A two-way tunnel
  and stairs have none; stairs say their way in their words. A closed or broken passage looks as in 1.2.81, with no words.
- **The outline your browser draws for a room** (the room a Monokuma's token stands in, and a found room's reveal) is cut where a
  secret passage of that floor runs in its wall, where the outline of a student who knows it is cut, and the cut is drawn again,
  dimmed, in the outline's colour, with no door glow. A room with no passage in its wall is outlined as in 1.2.81.
- Closing a passage draws the standing outline again whole, and opening it cuts it again, after a quarter of a second, with the
  outline's hop and the room's name, as a player's outline does when their passages change.
- The words, the arrowhead and the cut are drawn on every GM's browser, an Assistant GM's too, from the GMs' own rows, and on no
  player's, the Mastermind's player included. Nothing is sent and nothing is written for them.
- The words are drawn again a quarter of a second after a region is made, changed or deleted, a region behaviour is added or
  removed, or a scene's regions change, so they follow a moved room; this is read in the code and not driven by a test
  (LIVE-H82-03).

### For players

- **Your dice start as the GM's card arrives.** While a GM is connected, the dice of your action roll and of a statistic you
  click on your sheet now start when the GM's card for the roll reaches your browser, where 1.2.81 waited for the GM's answer,
  about one round trip later. In the harness, with 80 ms added each way on every browser, from your Roll to your dice: 495.1 ->
  327.8 ms for a statistic from the sheet and 545.8 -> 326.9 ms for an action's roll (medians of 10); with nothing added, 12.2 ->
  6.6 ms and 65.5 -> 5.9 ms.
- The dice fall once a roll: they do not fall again when the GM's answer comes, and without Dice So Nice the dice sound plays
  once. A roll the GM refuses throws nothing and tells you why once, as before. A hidden or private roll starts at the card only
  where your browser may read that card; elsewhere your dice start at the GM's answer, as in 1.2.81 (LIVE-H82-05).
- Your dice are now the roll on the GM's card, not your browser's own copy of it, so their Hope and Fear dice should look as on
  the GM's screen and the audience's; this has not been seen at a table (LIVE-H82-05).
- **With *One dice look for the table* on, your dice carry the GM's look and no special effects of your own:** the only effects
  on them are the ones a Gamemaster marks as global. An effect you pick in Dice So Nice goes back to none.
- **Your voice moves to the new room as soon as your move ends.** In the harness (scenario 75 I at 6b04250) the voice room was
  sent 3-8 ms after the move where 1.2.81 sent it 1507 ms after, and 5518 ms after while another character stepped inside their
  own room every second. A drag still on its way moves no voice, nor does another character's move while you drag, and a crossing
  the rules turn back moves it only to the room paid for, once (scenario 75 I; Known gaps).
- The voice tile's "Connecting" lasts as long as the voice connection itself, which this version does not change.

### For everybody

- **`game.drpg.perf()`** has a new line, "drawn for this browser, asked to dice started", beside "drawn for this browser, asked
  to dice shown", each with the answer's time in brackets. A table can read there whether a player's dice start before the GM's
  answer (LIVE-H82-05).
- With **Verbose console logging** on, each voice connect writes "Voice: the connect for "<room>" took N ms." in the console of
  the browser that connects, whatever its outcome, so the time the tile says "Connecting" can be read at a table (LIVE-H82-02).
- A roll whose dice started at the GM's card and which the GM's answer then calls not made leaves the Debug line "The dice of a
  roll the GM drew started at its message <id>, and the GM's answer says the roll was not made." on the roller's browser.
- **Why the dice waited.** The look back over the versions, booted one by one in the 1.2.81 harness with 80 ms added each way
  (ba6f366c to 1.2.67 in 1.2.67's own harness, and the request queue's timer patched in its copies of 1.2.64 to 1.2.75), measured
  Roll to dice at 162-166 ms from 1.2.50 to 1.2.66 and at 490-500 ms from 1.2.67 on, 580-650 ms on action rolls whose GM writes
  resources first. Since 1.2.67 the primary GM draws a player's action roll and statistic from the sheet, and the player's dice
  started only on the GM's answer, six one-way hops after the press, where the GM's card reaches the player at four. 1.2.79 and
  1.2.81 measure the same. The special effects 1.2.80 wrote on players hold the end of a throw in Dice So Nice, not its start
  (read in Dice So Nice 6.2.9's code, not measured). The look back also reads that from 1.2.62 to 1.2.77 the request queue's timer
  failed in a real browser (fixed in d69801d0, in 1.2.78), so on 1.2.67 to 1.2.77 a player's drawn roll rolled nothing, and it
  judges that the owner most likely first met the wait on 1.2.78.

## Changed

- No new file: 149 files in `scripts/`, as at 1.2.81.
- **The dice**: `dice-sync.mjs` (`lookFrom`, `canonicalLook`, `holdsTableLook`; `sourceLookOf` and `holdSource` keep the GM's
  whole list), `roll-draw.mjs` (`awaitStart`, `startWaitOf`, `startOnMessage`, `throwOnThisScreen`; `playBack` throws only where
  nothing started), `private-rolls.mjs` (`rollNonceOf` exported; `relayDrawnDice` still sends the dice to the audience and throws
  on the GM's screen only where nothing was shown) and `diagnostics.mjs` (the perf() line).
- **The voice**: `voice.mjs` (the updateToken hook: an immediate pass for a settled move, the 1500 ms pass kept behind it, none
  while a drag is in flight; the deleteToken hook forgets a deleted token's drag; `scheduleReconcile` unchanged),
  `voice-client.mjs` (the Debug line) and `movement.mjs` (`moveRefused`; voice.mjs now also waits on its existing `whenAtRest`).
- **The GMs' view of the passages**: `passages-gm.mjs` (`passageTunnels`, `endWords`, `wayArrow`, a redraw after a region
  change), `gm-overlay.mjs` (`clearLayer`), `passages.mjs` (`secretSegmentsOn`), `fog-doorways.mjs` (`gmPassageGaps`,
  `withPassageGhosts`, `floorWalls`, `traceGhostStretches`, `passageCutKey`, the cut in `traceOutlineGapped`; `doorwayEdges`
  unchanged), `fog-reveal.mjs` (`ghostStyle`, the dimmed cut in `flashOutline`, `recolour` and `rewidth`) and `fog.mjs` (one
  GM-only listener that draws the frame again).
- No bridge action and no socket action was added, and nothing a player sends is newly trusted: the roller starts its dice on
  the GM's own card, and the GM's screen throws the roll it has just evaluated.
- **Tests**: 10 new numbered tests, R940-R949 (4 in tier 0: R942, R945, R948 and R949; 6 in tier 1: R940, R941, R943, R944,
  R946 and R947); next free R950.
- The census rows of R379 and R553 changed with the new region listeners, and R611 compares a colour as R941 does.
- Two more tier-2 tests, which carry no number: "a player who holds the GM's dice effects as 1.2.80 wrote them has them taken off
  at the next sweep ..." and "a roll the GM drew whose message is not written was thrown once on the GM's screen ..." (956 titles
  in `scripts/tests-tier2.mjs`, 954 at 1.2.81); the tier-2 dice-look checks now ask for no effect.
- The scenario files are still 28: scenario 75 gains a phase I of 7 voice checks (its bound goes from 60 to 90 s), scenario 76
  gains a check T on the GM's words and two checks in C on the GM's outline, scenario 33 gains A17 (9 checks of a drawn roll on
  the player's and the GM's screens with 80 ms added each way), scenario 12's part without Dice So Nice holds the GM to one dice
  sound, and scenario 13's comments name where the roller's dice start.
- `known-leaks.json` is unchanged (9 known leaks).
- **The manifest's compatibility is unchanged**: Daggerheart `minimum` and `verified` 2.6.5, Foundry `minimum` 14.364 and
  `verified` 14.365.
- The handbooks, in English and Polish: the GM handbook's setting line for *One dice look for the table*, section 9.6 (a new
  "On a GM's board" bullet, and **Go through** no longer saying a GM's board draws no mark) and the perf() row; the player
  handbook's dice look line.
- Outside the module: `tools/stages.json` gains the E86 row and each unshipped 1.2.X row below it moves up one version (43 rows),
  `docs/dev/R-REGISTRY.md` gains the ten rows, and the audit's section 9.2 gains items 275 to 280 and rewords LIVE-E16-03.

## Known gaps

- **LIVE-H82-01** (not tried yet): with *One dice look for the table* on and the owner's own look with special effects,
  `game.drpg.perf()`'s "asked to dice shown" median from 10 player rolls on 1.2.81, on 1.2.81 with the setting off and on 1.2.82,
  and whether the wait came before the dice started or after they stopped; on 1.2.82 a player's and an Assistant GM's
  `sfxList` flag reads `[]`; a GM's global effect plays on a player's throw and a non-global one does not, with how
  `showOthersSFX` stands on each browser; whether a player's first throw after the look is put back is slower than the next.
- **LIVE-H82-02** (not tried yet): the "took" Debug line's ms for ten moves into another room, audio only and with a camera; from
  letting go of the token to the tile saying "Connecting"; a drag through several waypoints and a middle room ending in one
  connect; another player walking meanwhile; two separate moves about 1 s apart on 1.2.81 and on 1.2.82.
- **LIVE-H82-03** (not tried yet): the GM's words and arrowhead on a real board in both themes at play zoom, on an Assistant GM's
  and a second GM's browser, nothing on a player's or the Mastermind's, after a rename, a moved region and a floor switch.
- **LIVE-H82-04** (not tried yet): the GM's cut outline in both themes against the knower's, on an Assistant GM's and a second
  GM's browser, the redraw after a close and an open, and on a map where the knower's gap also depends on the room beyond or the
  move ray.
- **LIVE-H82-05** (not tried yet): at The Forge, the medians of "asked to dice started" and "asked to dice shown" from 10 action
  rolls and 10 statistics on a player's browser; the Hope and Fear dice's look against the GM's and the audience's; one throw a
  roll; forced private rolls; a refused roll; whether the "started at its message" Debug line ever appears.
- **LIVE-H82-06** (not tried yet): at The Forge, whether the GM's dice start noticeably sooner than on 1.2.81; one throw a roll on
  the GM's screen in the player's look; an Assistant GM and the audience as in 1.2.81; whether the dice stutter on a Fear result
  while the GM's browser counts Despair and redraws the HUD; whether the failed-write Debug line ever appears.
- LIVE-E16-03 now asks for the GM's appearance with the GM's global effects, not the GM's dice and effects.
- The time Dice So Nice holds a throw on its effects is not measured: the harness's Dice So Nice draws nothing and holds no throw,
  so R940 and the tier-2 test measure the flags only. That a Gamemaster's global effect plays on a player's throw, and only where
  the browser showing it is that Gamemaster's own or has `showOthersSFX` on, rests on reading Dice So Nice 6.2.9's code
  (Dice3D.js:140), not tried (LIVE-H82-01).
- The first throw after a look is put back may load the GM's dice preset then; this guess from the investigation is not
  addressed here (LIVE-H82-01).
- Two separate moves less than 1.5 s apart now reconnect a player's voice twice, where 1.2.81 made one pass; for two moves
  about 1 s apart, read from the code, this is faster than 1.2.81 only while a connect takes under 2.5 s (LIVE-H82-02). The owner
  decides whether a table feels it.
- If Foundry 14 does not mark a drag's steps as pending on the primary GM's copy of the token, a drag through a room reconnects
  voice there mid-drag; the harness marks them by hand (LIVE-H82-02, LIVE-E78-14, LIVE-E79-19).
- A crossing the rules let through and the charging browser then refuses for a budget that moved meanwhile still takes the
  immediate pass, so the mover's voice joins the refused room and comes back.
- A last step that Foundry 14 still marks as pending waits for the 1500 ms pass, as in 1.2.81.
- A token placed from the sidebar or by an Eclipse, and a token deleted, still wait 1500 ms for voice.
- The real voice reconnect (the tile's "Connecting") and the hops through the server at a table are not measured: the harness's
  stand-in connects at once over local IPC.
- A player's dice start early only where the GM's whispered card reaches the player's browser before the answer; where it does
  not, they start at the answer as in 1.2.81.
- A roll whose card the GM wrote and which then failed now shows its dice to the roller while the roller is told it was not
  made; no test drives a GM failing after its card.
- A primary GM that changes while a roll is out falls back to the answer's throw (read in the code, not driven).
- `perf()` has no line for the GM's own dice start, and `audit/live/perf-baseline.mjs` reads "asked to dice shown" only.
- The GM's screen throws its own evaluated roll, not the card's; faces and total are equal in scenario 33 A17 and the tier-2
  test, and the look of Daggerheart's Hope and Fear dice on it is not seen (LIVE-H82-06).
- A drawing GM that is no longer the primary when its card is created now shows the dice on its own screen at the throw, where it
  showed none (read in the code, not driven).
- Scenario 12 drives the GM without Dice So Nice for a statistic from the sheet only; an action's roll there takes the same branch
  and is not driven.
- The GM's words, arrowhead and cut are not seen headless: their look is chosen, not measured (words at alpha 0.7, the arrowhead
  grid x 0.3 by 0.24, the cut at alpha 0.35 under Monokuma Legacy and 0.6 under Stained Glass), the Legacy cut is never drawn
  headless, and an Assistant GM's and a second GM's board are not read headless.
- Until the reading of the rooms beyond has loaded at a GM's start, the rings are drawn with no words and then drawn again; how
  long that takes on Foundry 14 is not measured.
- The GM's words name the room beyond at the floor's bottom, a knower's mark at the token's height; a region whose height band
  leaves out the floor's bottom could name two different rooms (read in the code, not measured).
- The GMs' board does not hear a change of the player regions; it reads them at its next redraw.
- A GM's cut marks where the passage runs and leaves out the room beyond and the move ray a knower's gap also needs, so on some
  maps the two differ; measured equal only on scenario 76's Cafeteria (1225-1325) and R943's stand-ins (LIVE-H82-04).
- A second GM's outline and words follow another GM's change only if Foundry 14 tells that browser the GMs' rows changed, which is
  the harness's model only, and an outline drawn before the rows arrive is not drawn again otherwise.
- Every change of the GMs' passage rows that changes what cuts the standing outline replays its hop and the room's name on each
  GM's browser; the 250 ms wait is chosen, not measured.
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped are unchanged.
